items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had copied the first 8 measures of 'I Found You In Maytime' the way I heard Freddie Jenkins play it when I had heard him with Edgar Hayes in Kentucky.

ctx.x: Edgar started making piano rolls but I never heard any that he made. Another thing that Saughtercamp told Hayes the night that he sat at our dining room table was that Edgar had forgotten more piano than he (Saughtercamp) would ever be able to play. That was a great compliment for Edgar Hayes coming from a man who was considered the best white dance band pianist in our part of the country.

Lee Rainey had a model T Ford coupe 4 to go to work in. It was supposed to hold only 3 people, but 4 of us used to crowd into it. Edgar Hayes was living at Lee Rainey's house with a girl who was supposed to be his wife that he had brought from Kentucky. Her name was Ruby and she was a real fine frame. We finished work around 2 every morning and it would take us about an hour to get to the Sterling Hotel from the Woodlawn Inn.
